messages:
incident-bot: [CRITICAL] Hosted API queue growth detected in us-west-2. p99 latency > 12s for 6m; queue length 18k. Autoscaler reports repeated 'provisioner quota' errors. https://internal.redwood/alerts/3609991111 :rotating_light:
ops_sam: seeing it on the dashboard — CPU queues saturated too but GPU pools are the main hotspot. Autoscaler shows 502s from cloud provider when creating instances.
oncall-maya: I’m paged, looking now. Any customer-facing degradations?
seana_cs: multiple customers reporting timeouts, support tickets #CS-1104, #CS-1105. Estimated ~13% of Live traffic 504ing.
infra_eli: quick check: provisioner hitting cloud API rate limits + a soft cap on ephemeral GPUs in the account. Provisioner retries are in a tight loop and failing fast. Logs: ```time="2026-03-15T03:01:12Z" level=error msg="quota exceeded" provider=cloud region=us-west-2```.
eng_ryan: autoscaler attempted 24 node creations over 5m, ~70% failed. We got fallback to smaller model variants but routing didn't kick in because model-compat check timed out.
oncall-maya: can we tombstone some large batch jobs or pause low-priority workloads to free GPUs?
infra_eli: pausing background training jobs now — sending command to the job-controller: ```kubectl label job batch/priority-low pause=true --namespace=infra-tasks```
ops_sam: started evicting noncritical pods from the hosted-gpu pool (grace period 30s). Evictions should free ~6 GPUs in next 60s.
seana_cs: I'll update the affected customers with a one-liner. Anything actionable for them?
support_ana: telling customers we have degraded throughput, ETA unknown, advising retries/backoff. Ticket owners looped.
eng_ryan: immediate mitigation proposal: 1) temporary traffic-shift 10% -> eu-central-2-dedicated pool, 2) enable emergency autoscale override to bypass provisioner rate limit checks for 15m, 3) enable model-fallback to CPU-quantized variant for best-effort responses.
infra_eli: 1) can route 10% if Console route policy updated. I can flip it. 2) emergency override needs owner approval — I have creds. 3) CPU fallback is risky for latency but better than 504s.
ops_sam: do steps 1 and 3 first. Step 2 only if those don't reduce queue.
oncall-maya: agree. Run step 1 now?
infra_eli: doing traffic shift: ```/api/route-update --service=hosted-api --policy=weighted --weights=us-west-2:90,eu-central-2-dedicated:10 --auth-token=$OP_TOKEN```
deploy-bot: route-update started. Rollout id: r-3609991111-1. Progress: 0/10 -> 10/10 backends updated.
eng_ryan: enabling model-fallback on request path: ```PATCH /v1/configs/fallback -d '{"enabled":true,"percent":100,"model":"gpt-lite-cpu"}'``` - will convert queued requests to CPU fallback if GPU allocation fails.
infra_eli: fallback enabled. Note: these responses will have lower throughput and may increase p50 but reduce 504s.
ops_sam: queue length dropping slowly: 18k -> 11k in 2m. p99 down from 12s -> 5.8s. Good signal.
seana_cs: updating customers: "We’re seeing intermittent timeouts due to a GPU provisioning issue; we’ve routed some traffic to a secondary region and enabled degraded fallback to reduce errors. You may see slower responses for some requests."
eng_ryan: autoscaler still failing to create new GPU nodes; provider responses show throttling errors like `429 Client Throttle`. We need to request temporary quota bump with cloud support but that takes time.
infra_eli: opened cloud ticket CS-CL-711, ETA unknown. Meanwhile I can enable an autoscale 'burst' mode that re-uses warm standby instances: ```/infra/provisioner toggle-burst --pool=hosted-gpu --duration=15m``` — executing now.
oncall-maya: handoff note for next on-call: if p99 > 8s or queue > 8k re-escalate to infra lead and consider performing emergency tenant rate-limiting.
ops_sam: running a precautionary global token throttle to 85% of normal for non-enterprise tenants to reduce incoming pressure. Config: ```ratelimit set hosted-api global 0.85 --scope=non-enterprise```
support_ana: applying throttles may spike complaints but prevents wider outage. Sending proactive notice to top-affected customers.
eng_ryan: metrics now: queue 11k -> 6.5k over 6m, p99 ~4.2s, error rate down to 4.5%. Still above baseline.
seana_cs: customers on dedicated contracts unaffected; confirm?
infra_eli: confirmed dedicated pools untouched. Only hosted shared pools impacted.
oncall-maya: ok, I’ll stay on for the handoff. Who’s taking next 4-hour watch?
ops_sam: infra_eli will take 1st handoff, then eng_ryan for follow-up on autoscaler fixes.
infra_eli: acknowledged. Handoff summary: provisioner throttled by cloud API rate limiting and account GPU soft cap causing node creation failures. Mitigations: paused low-priority jobs, routed 10% traffic to eu-dedicated, enabled CPU fallback, toggled burst reuse, and applied non-enterprise client throttles. Open actions: request quota bump, add exponential backoff to provisioner retries, add earlier fallback trigger in routing policy, and postmortem.
seana_cs: logging CS impact: ~13% timed out, tickets opened, top customer affected ACME Corp (ticket CS-1104) — offered credits and status page updates.
oncall-maya: creating incident ticket INC-360999 with timeline and owners. Please add any missing notes.
eng_ryan: note: postmortem item: ensure model-compat timeout doesn't block fallback; we had a 4s model check timeout which caused traffic to stall.
ops_sam: reactions: :thumbsup: to infra_eli and eng_ryan, :heart: to support_ana for the customer comms.
infra_eli: taking over the watch. If anything regresses, ping me @infra_eli immediately.
seana_cs: sending final customer bulletin now.
support_ana: closing ticket hop for now; will reopen if error rate > 6% or queue grows.
incident-bot: Incident INC-360999 acknowledged and set to active. Pager duty assigned to infra_eli and eng_ryan.
oncall-maya: handing off to infra_eli — shifting to post-incident followups. Thanks all. :wave:
